legend: This is the hard version of the problem. The difference between the versions is that in this version, the path may end in any cave.
Henry went on an expedition into a network of caves in search of ancient artifacts. The entrance to the caves is at vertex 1%%ZSMJ0%%, and the corridors between caves form a tree.
Henry lights his way with a magic lamp. To pass through the i%%ZSMJ1%%-th corridor, the lamp spends wi%%ZSMJ2%% units of charge each time it is traversed.

However, the cave corridors are extremely unstable. After two traversals of the same corridor, its vault becomes too fragile, and it is impossible to use this corridor a third time. Therefore, Henry may traverse each corridor at most twice, regardless of the direction of movement.

There is an artifact in every cave. On the first visit to vertex v%%ZSMJ3%%, the artifact changes the lamp charge by av%%ZSMJ4%% units: some artifacts restore charge (those with av>0%%ZSMJ5%%), while others are cursed and instead take it away (av<0%%ZSMJ6%%). Visiting the cave again has no effect on the lamp charge.
At the beginning of the expedition, Henry is in cave 1%%ZSMJ7%% and immediately activates the artifact there. The lamp charge must never become negative at any moment.
Henry must visit all caves and collect all artifacts. After that, he can activate a portal in any cave and leave the dungeon, so he does not need to return to the entrance.
Determine the minimum initial lamp charge with which Henry can complete the expedition.
input: The first line contains one integer n%%ZSMJ8%% (1≤n≤2⋅105)%%ZSMJ9%% — the number of caves.

The second line contains n%%ZSMJ10%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ11%% (−109≤ai≤109)%%ZSMJ12%% — the changes in lamp charge after the first visit to the corresponding caves. Note that each corridor can be traversed at most twice, regardless of direction.

The next n−1%%ZSMJ13%% lines contain three integers each: ui%%ZSMJ14%%, vi%%ZSMJ15%%, and wi%%ZSMJ16%% (1≤ui,vi≤n, ui≠vi, 1≤wi≤109)%%ZSMJ17%% — the endpoints of the i%%ZSMJ18%%-th corridor and the amount of charge required to traverse it.
It is guaranteed that the corridors form a tree.
output: Print one integer — the minimum initial lamp charge with which Henry can visit all caves without the lamp charge ever becoming negative.

legend.ai: 这是本题的困难版本。两个版本的区别在于，在这个版本中，路径可以终止于任意洞穴。
Henry 深入一个洞穴网络探险，寻找古代文物。洞穴入口位于顶点 1%%ZSMJ0%%，洞穴之间的通道构成一棵树。
Henry用魔法灯照亮前路。穿过第 i%%ZSMJ1%% 条走廊时，灯每次都会消耗 wi%%ZSMJ2%% 单位电量。
然而，洞穴的通道极其不稳定。同一条通道在被经过两次后，其拱顶就会变得过于脆弱，无法第三次使用这条通道。因此，无论移动方向如何，Henry 最多只能经过每条通道两次。
每个洞穴中都有一个神器。第一次访问顶点 v%%ZSMJ3%% 时，神器会使灯的电量变化 av%%ZSMJ4%% 个单位：有些神器会恢复电量（那些 av>0%%ZSMJ5%% 的），而另一些则被诅咒，反而会消耗电量（av<0%%ZSMJ6%%）。再次访问该洞穴对灯的电量没有影响。
探险开始时，Henry 位于洞穴 1%%ZSMJ7%%，并立即激活了那里的神器。灯的充能值在任何时刻都绝不能变为负数。
Henry必须访问所有洞穴并收集所有神器。之后，他可以在任意洞穴中激活传送门并离开地牢，因此他无需返回入口。
求出 Henry 完成探险所需的最小初始提灯电量。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n%%ZSMJ8%% (1≤n≤2⋅105)%%ZSMJ9%% —— 洞穴的数量。
第二行包含 n%%ZSMJ10%% 个整数 a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ11%% (−109≤ai≤109)%%ZSMJ12%%——首次访问对应洞穴后灯的电量变化量。注意，每条走廊无论方向最多只能经过两次。
接下来的 n−1%%ZSMJ13%% 行每行包含三个整数：ui%%ZSMJ14%%、vi%%ZSMJ15%% 和 wi%%ZSMJ16%%（1≤ui,vi≤n, ui≠vi, 1≤wi≤109）%%ZSMJ17%% —— 第 i%%ZSMJ18%% 条走廊的两个端点以及通过它所需的电量。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——亨利能够访问所有洞穴且灯的电量始终不会变为负数所需的最小初始电量。
